star:sun.overview: The Sun (Sol) is a G2V main-sequence star at the center of the Solar System, containing about 99.86% of its total mass. With a diameter of approximately 1.39 million kilometers and a surface temperature around 5,500°C, it emits the energy that drives Earth’s climate and makes life possible. Energy is produced through nuclear fusion in its core, where temperatures reach roughly 15 million degrees Celsius. Formed about 4.6 billion years ago, the Sun is currently in a stable phase but will eventually evolve into a red giant in about 5 billion years. Sol is approximately 1,392,680 km across.
star:sun.observingGuide: Observe the Sun only with a certified front-aperture solar filter or a purpose-built solar telescope; unfiltered viewing can cause permanent eye damage.
star:sun.scienceContext: Useful scale comparisons are 109.298 Earth diameters, 27.94 g surface gravity. These values are rounded from the catalogue measurements shown on this page.

planet:mercury.overview: Mercury is the smallest and innermost planet of the Solar System, orbiting the Sun every 88 days. With almost no atmosphere, it experiences extreme temperature differences ranging from intense daytime heat to freezing nights. Its heavily cratered surface, including the massive Caloris Basin, preserves a record of early Solar System impacts. Despite its proximity to the Sun, Mercury contains water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters. Mercury is approximately 4,878 km across.

Venus is approximately 12,102 km across.
